_about: New verified records, 2026-11-24. Universities: on the NUC list of approved universities (existence and type); full profiles for three from Wikipedia. Schools: confirmed by their Wikipedia articles. Wording is our own.

u00.name: University of Nigeria, Nsukka
u00.h: The University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) is a federal university and the first indigenous, autonomous university in Nigeria. A law to set it up in the old Eastern Region was passed on 18 May 1955, championed by Nnamdi Azikiwe, who later became Nigeria's first president. Planners from the University of Exeter and Michigan State University surveyed the Nsukka site in 1958, and a provisional council chaired by Azikiwe was appointed in April 1959. The university formally opened on 7 October 1960, days after independence, as one of Nigeria's first-generation universities. It was modelled on the American system and was the first land-grant university in Africa, built around service to the country's practical needs.
u00.a: UNN is a public research university with 17 faculties and 102 academic departments, offering more than 108 undergraduate and 211 postgraduate programmes, including medicine, law, engineering, agriculture and the arts and sciences. It is regularly counted among the most respected universities in Nigeria.
u00.c: The main campus is in Nsukka, Enugu State. The university also has campuses in Enugu city and at Ituku-Ozalla in Enugu State, the site of its teaching hospital, and in Aba, Abia State.

u01.name: Lagos State University
u01.h: Lagos State University (LASU) is a public university owned by the Lagos State Government. It was established in 1983 during the administration of Governor Lateef Jakande, 'for the advancement of learning and establishment of academic excellence'. It was first conceived as a multi-campus, non-residential university, and it began with three faculties: Commerce and Business Administration, Law, and Medicine.
u01.a: LASU now serves more than 35,000 students and offers diploma, degree and postgraduate programmes, including an MBA. Faculties added over time include Arts, Education, Engineering, Social Sciences, Management Sciences, Science, and Communication and Media Studies, together with a School of Transport and a College of Medicine. It has hosted a World Bank Africa Centre of Excellence in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. Times Higher Education placed it among the world's top 600 universities in its 2020 rankings, and in 2021 named it the best young university in Nigeria.
u01.c: The main campus is at Ojo, on the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. The College of Medicine is at Ikeja, and the Epe campus, on the north side of the Lekki Lagoon, houses engineering, agriculture, environmental sciences and pre-degree studies.

u02.name: University of Medical Sciences, Ondo
u02.h: The University of Medical Sciences, Ondo (UNIMED) is a specialised public university owned by the Ondo State Government. It was created by a law signed in 2014 by Governor Olusegun Mimiko and approved by the National Universities Commission in 2015. It is described as the third specialised medical university in Africa, and it was the first specialised medical university in Nigeria to be accredited by the National Universities Commission. Its pioneer vice-chancellor was Professor Friday Okonofua, a gynaecologist and the founder of the Women's Health and Action Research Centre.
u02.a: UNIMED concentrates on medicine and the health sciences. It also runs an Institute of Community Health Innovation and Development.
u02.c: The university is in Ondo City, Ondo State, in south-western Nigeria.

s000.name: American International School of Lagos
s000.h: The American International School of Lagos (AISL) is an international school that follows an American curriculum, founded in 1964. It moved to its present campus on Victoria Island in 1981, on about 2.4 hectares (6 acres) of land leased from the government.
s000.a: AISL teaches students from preschool to grade 12, following the American system of education.
s000.c: The campus is on Victoria Island, Lagos.
s000.s: The school has more than 600 students. About 30 per cent are American, and the rest come from over 50 countries, with large groups from India, the United Kingdom, Nigeria, Canada, South Africa, Israel, Lebanon and the Netherlands.
s000.source_name: Wikipedia: American International School of Lagos

s001.name: Apata Memorial High School
s001.h: Apata Memorial High School is a privately owned school in Lagos run on military lines. It was founded in 1980 by S. O. Apata, a retired brigadier-general of the Nigerian Army.
s001.a: The school has about 1,550 pupils and 150 teachers, which gives it relatively small classes for a Lagos school of its size.
s001.s: It takes both boarding and day students, and its military-style discipline is part of daily life for boys and girls alike.

s002.name: Essence International School
s002.h: Essence International School (EIS) is an international school in Kaduna, founded in 1982.
s002.a: The school covers every stage of schooling: pre-nursery, nursery, primary and secondary education.
s002.c: It is on Kashim Ibrahim Road, near Sultan Road, in the Ungwan Rimi area of Kaduna.

s003.name: Air Force Military School, Jos
s003.h: Air Force Military School, Jos (AFMS) is a secondary school run by the Nigerian Air Force, established on 18 September 1980. By August 2022 it had graduated more than 3,794 'junior airmen', and many of its graduates have gone on to be commissioned officers in the army, air force and navy.
s003.a: AFMS combines a normal secondary curriculum, including subjects such as mathematics, physics, geography and French, with military training. Boys aged roughly 11 to 17 learn drill, map reading and interpretation, fieldcraft, compass and route marches, obstacle crossing, abseiling and weapons handling, as well as taking part in range practice, mock exercises and bush camps.
s003.c: The school is in Jos, Plateau State.
s003.s: Students are known as junior airmen, and the daily routine follows military discipline.
s003.source_name: Wikipedia: Air Force Military School, Jos

s004.name: Nigerian Navy Secondary School, Abeokuta
s004.h: The Nigerian Navy Secondary School, Abeokuta is an all-boys boarding school opened by the Nigerian Navy in 1990. By then, the Navy's only other secondary school, at Ojo in Lagos, could no longer take all the children of naval personnel who wanted places. The governor of Ogun State, Captain Mohammed Lawal, suggested the site of the defunct St Leo's Teachers' Training College at Ibara, Abeokuta, and the Navy appointed the school's first staff on 20 November 1990.
s004.a: The school offers academic secondary education together with military-style training. Admiral Murtala Nyako directed that, although it is a civilian school, it should be run as the equivalent of a military school.
s004.c: The campus is on the hilly Onikolobo site at Ibara, Abeokuta, Ogun State.
s004.source_name: Wikipedia: Nigerian Navy Secondary School, Abeokuta

s005.name: Indian Language School
s005.h: The Indian Language School is a school in Lagos founded in 1982 to serve the city's growing Indian community. It comes under the High Commission of India in Nigeria and is managed by a board of trustees of business people. It began in converted houses at 11 Johnson Street, Ilupeju, and has since expanded by acquiring neighbouring properties. It is the only Indian school in Lagos.
s005.a: The school teaches from lower kindergarten to the 12th standard, and has entered students for the Indian CBSE board examinations for grades 10 and 12 since the late 1980s.
s005.c: The school is at Johnson Street, Ilupeju, Lagos, with a playground and football, basketball and volleyball courts.

s006.name: Loyola College, Ibadan
s006.h: Loyola College, Ibadan (LCI) is a boys' secondary school founded by Catholic missionaries in 1954 and now owned by the Oyo State Government. It has produced alumni in medicine, engineering, law, politics and the media.
s006.a: Students sit the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) at the end of senior secondary school. Old students support the school: in October 2023, for example, an alumnus paid the WAEC fees of six final-year students and sponsored UTME candidates.
s006.c: The college is on Old Ife Road in the Agodi area of Ibadan, Oyo State.

s007.name: St Anne's School, Ibadan
s007.h: St Anne's School, Ibadan is a girls' secondary school that can claim to be the oldest girls' secondary school in Nigeria. It traces its history to the CMS Female Institution, founded in Lagos on 1 May 1869 at the urging of Abigail Macaulay, daughter of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, so that Lagos families need not send their daughters abroad to study. That school, later the CMS Girls School, merged in 1950 with Kudeti Girls School in Ibadan, founded in 1899. The combined school was renamed St Anne's in honour of the missionary Anna Hinderer.
s007.a: The school started with sixteen pupils on what is now Broad Street, Lagos, under its first principal, Mrs Roper, and today provides secondary education for girls.
s007.c: The school is in Ibadan, Oyo State.

s008.name: Ijebu Ode Grammar School
s008.h: Ijebu Ode Grammar School (JOGS) is a boys' secondary school founded on 20 January 1913, which makes it one of the oldest secondary schools in Nigeria. The educationist Israel Oludotun Ransome-Kuti is among the figures associated with its history.
s008.a: The school provides junior and senior secondary education for boys.
s008.c: It is in Ijebu-Ode local government area of Ogun State, south-western Nigeria.
s008.s: Students belong to six houses: Gansallo (blue), Johnson (red), Kuti (grey), Odumosu (green), Phillips (yellow) and School (purple).

s009.name: Olivet Baptist High School
s009.h: Olivet Baptist High School, formerly Oyo Baptist Boys' High School, is a Baptist secondary school affiliated with the Nigerian Baptist Convention. American Baptist missionaries founded it on 29 January 1945 in the old Baptist mission house at Oke-Isokun, Oyo, where the first Baptist missionary to Oyo had set up a mission post; that site is now the Baptist College of Theology. The school was widely known in the 1960s for excellence in both academics and sport.
s009.a: Olivet once prepared students for both O-level and A-level (Higher School Certificate) examinations; the A-level programme ended in 1989. It was one of the few schools outside Lagos with laboratories for the sciences, home economics, fine arts and music, and workshops for metalwork, woodwork and technical drawing.
s009.c: The school stands on a hilltop known as Olivet Heights in Oyo town, Oyo State, with hostels and staff quarters on campus.

s010.name: Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran
s010.h: Lagos State Model Junior College, Meiran is a state-owned junior secondary school. It was formed on 6 January 2003, when the Lagos State Ministry of Education split every secondary school in the state into separate junior (JSS1–3) and senior (SS1–3) schools. It came from Lagos State Model College, Meiran, founded on 19 February 1988; the same reform created junior model colleges at Badore, Igbonla, Kankon and Igbokuta. Its first principal, Mrs T. D. Kuti, led it until 2009.
s010.a: As a junior college it teaches the first three years of secondary school (JSS1 to JSS3), after which students move to senior secondary school.
s010.c: The school is at Oke-Odo, Meiran, in the north of Lagos.
s010.source_name: Wikipedia: Lagos State Model Junior College Meiran

s011.name: American International School of Abuja
s011.h: The American International School of Abuja (AISA) is a co-educational international day school founded in 1993 by a group of parents and US Embassy officials. They wanted a school that would prepare international and Nigerian students to continue their education under an American curriculum. In August 2006 it moved into a new purpose-built campus with room to grow.
s011.a: AISA teaches from preschool to grade 12, following a US-based curriculum, over a school year that runs from August to June with 180 teaching days. As enrolment grew from about 150 students in 2005 to about 470, it added a full high school programme.
s011.c: The school is in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory.
s011.s: Its students come from more than 40 countries.
s011.source_name: Wikipedia: American International School of Abuja

s012.name: Binta International School
s012.h: Binta International School is part of a group of schools founded by Mrs Ehi Adenuga in Lagos. It opened in Ejigbo in 1994 and later moved to Ajao Estate, Isolo. Its name stands for 'Best In Nurturing Talents and Academics', its motto is 'excellence and discipline', and it gave its name to the school in the national television series Binta and Friends.
s012.a: The group runs a crèche, nursery, basic school and high school, and awards scholarships to deserving students each year. Its students have won competitions including the AIT Whizkid competition (1995), the 12th Unilever essay competition and the AIT debate competition (both 2000), and placed second in the Cowbell Lagos secondary school mathematics competition.
s012.c: The school is in Ajao Estate, Isolo, Lagos.

s013.name: A.D.R.A.O. International School
s013.h: A.D.R.A.O. International School is a co-educational international school founded in 1963 by Chief Abimbola Omololu-Mulele. It is one of the oldest independent schools in Nigeria.
s013.a: The school provides independent, international-style education for boys and girls.
s013.c: The school is on Victoria Island, Lagos.

s014.name: Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro
s014.h: Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro was founded in February 1963 by the government of the old Western Region, as an experiment in linking secondary education to the country's manpower needs after independence. It was set up with American support: Harvard University staff came through USAID, and the Ford Foundation funded the school until 1973. Similar comprehensive schools were proposed for Nigeria and Kenya at the same time.
s014.a: The school was designed to combine academic and practical education, giving priority to sixth-form science and adding technical streams at school-certificate level, unlike the purely academic grammar schools of the time.
s014.c: It is in Ayetoro, in the Egbado (Yewa) area of Ogun State, south-western Nigeria.

s015.name: Lycée Français Louis Pasteur de Lagos
s015.h: The Lycée Français Louis Pasteur de Lagos (LFLP) is a French international school established in 1958 by the Association Française du Nigeria. It operated from several sites in Ikoyi and Victoria Island before moving in 1987 into purpose-built premises funded with support from the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and it took the name Lycée Français in 1997.
s015.a: The school teaches the French national curriculum from primary through secondary school. It belongs to the Agency for French Education Abroad (AEFE), the worldwide network of French schools.
s015.c: The school is on Victoria Island, Lagos.
s015.source_name: Wikipedia: Lycée Français Louis Pasteur de Lagos

s016.name: Wesley College of Science, Ibadan
s016.h: Wesley College of Science, Ibadan was founded as Wesley College on 5 November 1905. It was originally a teacher-training institution, and one of its best-known students was Chief Obafemi Awolowo, the first premier of the Western Region. It is often described as one of the oldest secondary schools in Nigeria.
s016.a: Today it is a government-controlled, co-educational senior secondary school that prepares science students for the Senior School Certificate Examination.
s016.c: The college is in Ibadan, Oyo State.
s016.source_name: Wikipedia: Wesley College of Science, Ibadan

s017.name: School for the Gifted, Gwagwalada
s017.h: The School for the Gifted, Gwagwalada, formerly Government Gifted Secondary School, is a public secondary school established in 1993 to meet the educational needs of gifted students in the Federal Capital Territory. It began operating in 1994, and its motto is 'Knowledge for Excellence'.
s017.a: The school offers science, humanities and business streams at senior secondary level.
s017.c: It is in Gwagwalada, in the Federal Capital Territory.
s017.source_name: Wikipedia: School for the Gifted, Gwagwalada

s018.name: Mount Saint Gabriel's Secondary School
s018.h: Mount Saint Gabriel's Secondary School (MSG) is a Catholic boys' boarding school founded on 14 January 1964 by Bishop James Hagan of the Catholic Diocese of Makurdi. It was the first secondary school in Makurdi. It opened as a day school with 63 boys from Tiv, Idoma, Igbo, Hausa and other communities, in temporary classrooms at Holy Ghost Parish, and moved to its permanent site in 1966. The Nigerian Civil War slowed its growth, but it recovered and expanded in the 1970s.
s018.a: MSG follows the national curriculum and prepares students for WAEC and NECO examinations, and it is known for academic excellence in Benue State.
s018.c: The school is in Makurdi, the capital of Benue State, near Government College.
s018.source_name: Wikipedia: Mount Saint Gabriel's Secondary School

s019.name: Grundtvig International Secondary School
s019.h: Grundtvig International Secondary School is an independent boarding school founded in 1998 by Dr Kachi E. Ozumba (1942–2011). It is named after the Danish philosopher N. F. S. Grundtvig and is built on his 'education for life' folk high school ideas.
s019.a: The school educates boys and girls aged 12 to 18. It has repeatedly been among the top ten schools in Nigeria by WAEC results, ranking fifth in 2014. On 5 October 2020 it received the Presidential Award as the overall best private secondary school in Nigeria, in the President's Teachers' and Schools Excellence Awards.
s019.c: The school is in Oba, Anambra State, about twenty minutes' drive from Asaba Airport.

s020.name: Charles Dale Memorial International School
s020.h: Charles Dale Memorial International School (CDMIS) is a secondary boarding school affiliated with Bereton Montessori School. Bereton's leadership decided, at its 25th anniversary in 2003, to open a secondary school so that pupils could continue their education there. Ground was broken in 2004, and the school opened on 30 September 2006. It is named in memory of Charles Dale for his contribution to education in Nigeria.
s020.a: The school has about 400 students and more than 45 teaching staff.
s020.c: The campus is at 12 Army Range Road, Igwuruta-Eneka, Port Harcourt, Rivers State. It has science and computer laboratories, a library, sports fields, and housing for students and staff.
s020.source_name: Wikipedia: Charles Dale Memorial International School

s022.name: Olashore International School
s022.h: Olashore International School is a private, co-educational boarding secondary school founded in 1994 by the late Oba Olashore. In January 2022 its board of trustees set up a five-member panel to investigate allegations about how the school handled a 2004 case of sexual assault involving its students; no findings had been published at the time the source was written.
s022.a: The school teaches both the Nigerian and British curricula, preparing students for examinations including the Cambridge IGCSE and the West African Senior School Certificate Examination.
s022.c: The school occupies a 60-hectare campus at Iloko-Ijesa, Osun State, about three hours' drive from Lagos.

s023.name: Mater Amabilis Secondary School
s023.h: Mater Amabilis Secondary School is a Catholic boarding high school run by the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Onitsha. It was founded on 15 January 1962 by Archbishop Charles Heerey. Its roots go back to 1905, when the traditional ruler of Umuoji, Igwe Okafor Ugwumba, invited Irish Catholic missionaries to the town. Bishop Joseph Shanahan sent the catechist Jacob Chukwuemeka Odiakosa, who built the Umuoji parish, and in the 1950s the parish priest, Father John Jordan, founded Our Lady's Teacher Training College there.
s023.a: The school provides Catholic secondary education with boarding.
s023.c: It is in Umuoji, Anambra State.

s024.name: Lumen Christi International High School
s024.h: Lumen Christi International High School is a Catholic boys' boarding school founded on 5 October 1986 by Patrick Ekpu, later Archbishop Emeritus of Benin. It is owned and run by the Catholic Diocese of Uromi.
s024.a: The school has a record in competitions and examinations. It won the Edo State Governorship Debate Award on 30 September 2015, and that year one of its graduates was named the overall best NECO candidate in Edo State. It has also won the LAPO science quiz competition.
s024.c: The school is at Ivue, Irrua, in Esan Central local government area, in the Esan heartland of Edo State.
s024.source_name: Wikipedia: Lumen Christi International High School

s025.name: Government College Ikorodu
s025.h: Government College Ikorodu is a co-educational public secondary school founded on 21 September 1974 and formally opened two days later by Brigadier Mobolaji Johnson, then governor of Lagos State. About 200 pioneer students were transferred from other Lagos secondary schools on the basis of that year's common entrance examination, and the school first used a temporary site on Obafemi Awolowo Way (then Agbowa Road). Its first principal was Olatunde Balogun.
s025.a: The college did well in its first years: in 1975 it was among five colleges whose students received scholarships from the commissioner for education, Chief Adeniran Ogunsanya.
s025.c: The college is in Ikorodu, Lagos State.

s027.name: Bridge House College
s027.h: Bridge House College (BHC) is an independent, co-educational sixth-form college established in 2004 to prepare school leavers aged 15 to 19 for university. It started with eight students who wanted to study in the United Kingdom. From 2007 it began preparing students for universities in other countries as well, including the US, Canada, the UAE, Ireland, Ghana and Nigeria.
s027.a: The college teaches Cambridge A levels, with a one-year AS route and a two-year A2 route. It is an accredited Cambridge examination centre and offers Cambridge teacher training. It has educated more than 2,500 students, including the children of expatriates living in Nigeria.
s027.c: The college began on Olagunsoye Oyinlola Street, 2nd Avenue, Ikoyi, Lagos, and moved to its permanent campus in 2014.

s028.name: Marygold International School
s028.h: Marygold International School is a private, co-educational boarding and day school founded in 2002 by Obinna and Janeth Weli.
s028.a: The school covers every stage from crèche, toddler, pre-nursery and nursery through primary to secondary school, with departments for science, music, ICT, phonics and vocational studies.
s028.c: Its main building is at 58 Station Road, Elelenwo, Port Harcourt, Rivers State.
